To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new acridone derivate 2-amino-acetamido-10(3, 5dimethoxybenzyl)-9(10H)acridone hydrocloride, named 8a, synthesized in our lab, shows potent antitumoral activity.
the acridine derivative 8a can induce oxidative stress-mediated apoptosis and that the UPLC/QTOF MS based metabonomic approach provides novel insights in the mechanistic studies.
the acridine derivative 2-amino acetamido-10(3,5-dimetoxi-benzil)-9(10H)acridona hydrochloride induces apoptosis in leukemia cells by oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the study of the mechanisms of antitumor compounds.
the application of metabolomic approaches to the study of the antitumor mechanism.
the development of novel antitumor agents and the application of metabolomics in mechanism studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antitumor activity of 8a is mainly attributed to its ability to induce ROS generation, which in turn leads to the activation of caspases, resulting in the apoptosis of CCRF- CEM leukemia cells.
8a induces cell apoptosis by increasing ROS production, which is followed by the activation of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway and the caspase-dependent apoptotic pathway.
the acridine derivative 8a exerts its potent antitumor effect by inducing oxidative stress-mediated apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolomic approach is a powerful tool for elucidating the mechanism of action of antitumor agents.
metabolomics is a powerful tool for studying drug mechanisms and for guiding drug design.
we have developed a new antitumor drug candidate 8a and revealed its mechanism of action by metabolomics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UPLC/QTOF MS metabolomics approach is a promising strategy to investigate the mechanism of antitumor agents and to discover new biomarkers for cancer diagnosis.

metabolomics can be used in the early stages of antitumor drug development to screen for compounds with potential antitumor activity and to provide a better understanding of their antitumor mechanism.
UPLC/QTOF MS based metabolic profiling could be a promising tool for the mechanistic studies and drug development of antitumor agents.
